newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond spreads flat, junk telecoms up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond spreads flat, junk telecoms up.

text.p: U.S. high-grades debt dealers reported a mild pickup in bidding activity at midday following the Federal Reserve's decision the leave short-term rates unchanged, players said.
Prices were quoted higher in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries and spreads were mostly unchanged, traders said. Dealers said volume was subdued but there was moderate retail interest.

Junk trade was again focused on high-yielding telecoms, including Nextel Communication's zero coupon senior discount notes due 2003. Nextel debt rose 3/4 point by midday after trading up more than one point to 72-3/4 bid on Tuesday.
One trader at a big New York shop said players were setting shorts in Nextel stock and buying the bonds.

Investors refocused on telecoms after recent underperformance, spurred by the bullish tone fostered over the past week, an analyst said. The favorable environment will likely spur another bolt of zero telecom deals to market in the near future, the analyst said.

In the high-yield new issue market, E&S Holdings Corp's $200 million senior subordinated notes, priced at par to yield 10.375 percent late on Tuesday, popped up to a 101-1/2 bid early on Wednesday, traders said.
The E&S deal was termed "a blowout" by analysts, the debt underpinned by strong Kohlberg, Kravitz Roberts & Co parentage and assets of Spalding & Evenflo Companies Inc.
Other high-yield issuance also included Ocwen Financial Corp's $125 million notes due 2003, priced at par to yield 11.875 percent. The bonds are rated B1 and B-plus.
Back in investment grades, traders reported a plethora of inquiries but spotty trades.
ATT Corp debt was inactive but lagged the uptick following news Tuesday the firm's third-quarter profit would fall below expectations. One trader said the debt was overvalued.
High-grades issuance on Wednesday will feature $250 million Coca-Cola Enterprises via lead manager Lehman Brothers, syndicate sources said.
The issue consists of a 30-year bond with a put option in the 10th year. Price talk is 33 to 36 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury, sources added.
The issue is rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and AA-minus by Standard & Poor's.

In the governments market, the benchmark 30-year bond was quoted up 19/32 to 97-20/32 to yield 6.94 percent at 1304 EDT/1704 GMT. Short covering and central bank buying of two- and five-year notes boosted prices, analysts said
